title: Emrys and the Spire
premise: Lena Halloran survives as a royal food-taster and secret ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, a shadowy covenant that once bound the mortal realm to the Spire, a frozen tower where memory is currency. When she discovers tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies naming her as the Covenant-Bearer, she is seized by the Spire's warden and forced to confront the truth: her guild has been quietly selling memories to keep the long winter at bay, dooming the realm's past to oblivion. Refusing to be either savior or sacrifice, Lena bargains with the warden using the one thing no prophecy accounted for — her own recorded ledgers of every debt the realms owe each other. In the climax she reforges the broken covenant not with blood but with balanced accounts, trading her immunity and her memories of survival for an endless spring. She wakes with no ledger in hand and no memory of why she flinches at certain dishes, yet the winter has stopped falling, and somewhere a new book of prophecies begins writing itself.
about_author: Gideon Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing debts, wills, and unfulfilled promises in a northern port city. They write fantasy about people who keep records of things everyone else would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Taster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. By day she tastes the king's food, building immunity dish by dish; by night she balances the Guild of Impossible Things' ledgers, entries that trade in years, names, and borrowed luck. When she finds tonight's date inked in a prophecy book older than the guild itself — beside her own name — she barely has time to hide the ledger before the Spire's warden steps out of the pantry cold. Beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Winter Eats
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, deep in the Spire. The warden shows her the covenant's cost: each winter fed on surrendered memories, and the guild's elders have been selling the realm's past to postpone the final frost. Lena realizes her ledgers hold the only complete record of what both realms owe. An old guildsman arrives to silence her; she escapes deeper into the tower with the prophecy book. Beat: betrayal curdling into defiance.

chapters.title: A Balance Owed
chapters.summary: Lena's POV at the covenant's shattered heart. The warden offers her the prophesied role: die as the Covenant-Bearer and buy one more century. Instead she opens her ledgers and audits the covenant itself, proving the realms' debts nearly cancel — if someone pays the difference. The guildsman returns with the elders; the long winter breaks through the Spire walls mid-negotiation. Beat: terror transfigured into audacity as she names her price.

chapters.title: Spring, Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, then a coda from the warden's. She signs herself into the covenant as the balancing entry, surrendering her immunities and her memories of every survival the ledgers record. The winter stops mid-fall; the Spire thaws into a garden of returned names. She wakes in the palace kitchens, a taster again, flinching at dishes she can't explain — while far away, a blank prophecy book writes its first line. Beat: grief braided with hard-won peace.
